@GeoffreyBooth I did not realize this utility might be sensitive and at a bigger scope, my apologies for not tagging the relevant groups.

> There is already an `--import` flag that can accept either a CommonJS or an ESM file or package. I would expect `--test` and `--test-reporter` to essentially be aliases of that, without needing any new modules infrastructure like requireOrImport

`-- test` is used for spawning a child process so it is treated as the main module (as it was prior to this PR) so the discussion is mainly in regards to `--test-reporter`

> We should also discuss the expected outputs from these files; it seems like you’re expecting whatever `--test-reporter` points to to provide a default export that’s a function that’s the test reporter, but this means that the user is forced to declare the test reporter via this new flag. An alternative API that wouldn’t involve a few flag or import code path would be something like `import { registerTestReporter } from 'node:test'; registerTestReporter(testReporterFunction)`. Such an API would eliminate the need for changes to the modules system, I would think. (It might not be your desired UX, which I completely understand, but we could discuss various options.)

The API implemented here was discussed at https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/45648 mainly by @nodejs/test_runner so I don't think we will want to change how it works in the high-level (mainly in regards to matching a `--test-reporter` with a `--test-reporter-destination`)
the main challenge with the API you have suggested (similar propositions were raised for other test runner configurations) is that the test runner resides in multiple processes so cherry-picking what configuration belongs to which process is not trivial 

> In the near term, could the changes to lib/internal/modules from this PR please be reverted?

If you are fine with that - I would prefer to revert the utility to currently only supporting CJS reporters and once we come up with a solution in https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/45648 we can support both CJS and ESM

> If you are fine with that - I would prefer to revert the utility to currently only supporting CJS reporters and once we come up with a solution in #45648 we can support both CJS and ESM

I don’t like the idea of supporting only CJS reporters, and I feel like there would be similar “import flow” issues to sort out with that too. Could we perhaps just revert this for now? It only just landed today. We can open a new PR to hash out the module loading stuff, and then re-land.

> I don’t like the idea of supporting only CJS reporters, and I feel like there would be similar “import flow” issues to sort out with that too. 

I am not proposing to never support ESM reporters, that was only suggested as an intermediate step.

> Could we perhaps just revert this for now? It only just landed today. We can open a new PR to hash out the module loading stuff, and then re-land.

this PR was open for almost three weeks and reviewed by more than 2 collaborators, according to the process, so I am not sure why it should be reverted rather than opening a PR fixing the specific issue around ESM reporters.

👍 on iterating and improving rather than reverting. This isn't even in a release yet, it's an experimental API and it's very valuable to get feedback from users/collaborators.

Feedback from the loaders team would be very valuable to iterate on this feature and I think it would be great if @GeoffreyBooth collaborated with @MoLow on improving this.

I am also +0.5 on adding a "this API can and will break whenever core feels like it" warning in case the "Non-backward compatible changes or removal may occur in any future release. Use of the feature is not recommended in production environments." warning isn't sufficient.

> specific issue around ESM reporters.

It's not just ESM. This PR refactors part of the entry point handler before either the CJS or ESM loaders are chosen. The new flag should be piping all reporters through the ESM loader, even CommonJS reporters, so that the Loaders API can apply to them.

Reverting and reopening is more of a courtesy to allow the relevant teams time to review without the pressure that this gets released or backported or further built upon.

> It's not just ESM. This PR refactors part of the entry point handler before either the CJS or ESM loaders are chosen. The new flag should be piping all reporters through the ESM loader, even CommonJS reporters, so that the Loaders API can apply to them.

Is there a regression or semantic change in the behaviour for CJS/ESM loading for anything other than test reporters because of this PR?
I think we should revert the changes related to modules and only support CJS until an acceptable ESM approach is figured out.

> Is there a regression or semantic change in the behaviour for CJS/ESM loading for anything other than test reporters because of this PR?

The changes to the modules code impede some initiatives we have in progress. In https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45828 and https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45659 @joyeecheung is working on moving more of the module loader into the build snapshot. Part of that is merging together small files, rather than creating new ones; and also separating logic that belongs in the snapshot (stuff used by most Node users) from code that should be lazy-loaded (everything else). `shouldUseESMLoader` is used by 100% of Node users on startup so it absolutely belongs in the snapshot, but `requireOrImport` is only used to support the test runner. These functions shouldn’t be in the same file.

If you look closer at `shouldUseESMLoader`, it’s not just determining whether an entry point is a CommonJS file or an ESM file; there are other conditions that also cause the ESM loader to be selected to process the entry point. This is because the ESM loader could _always_ be used, since it can handle either CommonJS or ESM files; the only reason it currently isn’t is because of some exposed internals async activity that async hooks pick up. https://github.com/nodejs/node/discussions/45711 is a discussion to sketch out what needs to happen to overcome this limitation, so that we can finish merging the ESM and CommonJS loaders. We already opt into the ESM loader whenever we can without breaking async hooks, regardless of whether we _have_ to; that’s why `shouldUseESMLoader` returns `true` if `--import` is used, even if `--import` is referencing a CommonJS file, for example. `--test-reporter` should function the same way: it should always load test reporters through the ESM loader. It looks to me like `requireOrImport` is trying to determine if the test reporter is CommonJS or ESM, and therefore to load it via one loader or the other; it should just send everything through the ESM loader. I would think we probably don’t need the `requireOrImport` function at all.

https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45916 introduces modules changes around passing through a parent URL that I don’t fully understand. I’m a lot less concerned about these; if the module loader isn’t passing along a correct reference to a parent module, then it should. But I would suggest that such changes be their own PR, with their own tests, and not bundled into a larger test runner-related PR. These _could_ be changes that affect real users; users look for the lack of a parent in a module as a way to know that it’s the entry point, and we might not have enough tests to cover all the ways that users do so. That’s why I want such a change to be an isolated PR so it can get more attention, including from loaders authors who are the ones most likely to be relying on the current behavior.

> I think we should revert the changes related to modules and only support CJS until an acceptable ESM approach is figured out.

This feature isn’t behind a flag. I’m not okay with features lacking ESM support being landed without both an experimental flag and an experimental warning, if not a build flag as well. More broadly though, I don’t like the idea of deferring ESM support until later, which may never come. We should just figure it out correctly the first time.

If you want a temporary solution, `import { registerTestReporter } from 'node:test'; registerTestReporter(testReporterFunction)` is one. It would support both CJS and ESM, and arguably it’s not a bad thing to have for the long term in addition to a `--test-reporter` flag. If you want to potentially remove it later when the flag is ready, add an `--experimental-test-runner` flag to enable `import { registerTestReporter } from 'node:test'` and a warning that doesn’t just say that test reporters are experimental but also that they might change at any time. Or you could add an `--experimental-test-runner` flag, that is required to enable the entire test runner, to emphasize to users that this is a work-in-progress and will likely have breaking changes before it becomes stable. The test runner isn’t in the “baking” phase, and arguably it shouldn’t be so easy to access since that implies to users that it’s stable or nearly so.
It’s actually almost trivial to revert the module system changes without breaking anything, even the new `--test-reporter`: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45923.

> We should just figure it out correctly the first time.

This feels like the same sentiment I've expressed in many PR reviews, which has been pushed back on (by you and others) because node's ethos, driven by the TSC, is *not* to figure it out correctly the first time, but rather to iterate over time, using experimental status and flags as needed.

I thought there were recent discussions around not holding back features for one module system just because it doesn't support the other, but I can't recall where they were held atm.

> I have to echo Geoffrey though: This changed code under the shared purview of the loaders and modules teams (among others). I'm sure there was not ill intention, but we should have been consulted/tagged

If the module team wants code to _actually_ be under the purview of it rather than the collaborator base it should:

 - Get chartered by the TSC with charter that explicitly state the process
 - Set up automation to tag the team in changes that touch files in these folders

Otherwise, I disagree anything wrong was done here process wise. As you mention there was no ill intent, the same process as all the other code was used, it was open for 3 weeks and wasn't rushed etc.

Here the module/loader changes were adjusted according to the feedback because of (positive) collaboration between Moshe and Geoffrey (and others) and because both felt strongly about figuring this out and adjusting the result.

In the future when I see test runner PRs touching these files I will tag the loaders team but that is a courtesy because I like the team and find the feedback valuable but if that should be the process we should change the process.

> * Set up automation to tag the team in changes that touch files in these folders

This exists; that’s how I found out about this, because it happened on the follow-up: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45916#issuecomment-1358629625. I’m not sure why the automation didn’t get triggered for this PR; maybe because percentage-wise so little of this PR was modules-related rather than test runner-related? But my preference would be that modules-related changes always ping @nodejs/modules.

There isn’t a modules team at the moment; it was disbanded after the ESM effort (long story). The loaders team is the de facto modules team, as most modules development these days is related to loaders.
Thanks for clarifying, my experience in virtually every area outside of modules (and promises back then) is that the limiting factor is people willing to engage, review code and provide feedback.

> I have to echo Geoffrey though: This changed code under the shared purview of the loaders and modules teams (among others). I'm sure there was not ill intention, but we should have been consulted/tagged (had we been and we ignored it, sure, that's on us). This (unintentionally, I'm sure) was counter-productive to multiple on-going, well broadcasted, cross-team efforts.

And I have to echo Benjamin, I disagree anything wrong was done here process wise.
I don't really appreciate you calling this counter-productive, let's not forget Node.js is run by volunteers, and if we start making such comments on PRs that landed, it would very likely drive contributors away, and that wouldn't be very productive, would it? Sure I should have thought of pinging the teams when reviewing, and I understand that can be frustrating for you, but I'm only human, the project can't expect that I would always remember what teams to ping and when. It's ok to criticize the process, of course, and/or to suggest ways to improve it, but please let's not make judgement calls on the productivity of contributions when there's no bad faith involved.

(if you think it's unreasonable to expect that you would watch every open PRs to see what code you'd like to review, similarly it's unreasonable to expect others to ping you on every PRs that would interest you. The solution is automation, and as said above there's already something in place – but that would need to be improved as it didn't catch this one, PR welcome I suppose).

Preface: When I wrote my initial message here I had not seen all of the other chatter around this (it was collapsed). My message did not post for some hours after (I assume my mobile lost wifi or I closed the app too fast and then the message got posted when I next opened the app). Seeing all the rest, I see I ended up beating a dead horse (it was already addressed/resolved—sorry for that).

---

I should have said "somewhat" counter-productive; it objectively was, so I'm surprised that caused upset. I thought my general tone was appreciative of Moshe's contribution (because I literally said so) with a minor addendum of "this created a small, but avoidable problem, and it's 'bad' because x, y, z". My intention was merely to provide actionable feedback with clear rationale. I also thought I was making it clear I felt it was an understandable oversight (if touching ESM code, probably a good idea to give them a heads up—similarly if I touched test's code, I _should_ give them a heads up too, even if I'm not strictly required to do).

> in virtually every area outside of modules (and promises back then) is that the limiting factor is people willing to engage, review code and provide feedback.

Not sure if I'm grouped into the ones who you're saying you can rely on to collab, but AFAIK, I've never not reviewed a PR on which it was requested, nor never not participated in a collaboration in which it was solicited. I especially would not ignore a request from a contributor who had collaborated with me. I hope you (and Antoine and Moshe) know I would not neglect to provide any of those for you.

> Sure I should have thought of pinging the teams when reviewing

No-no, I wasn't criticising you (or the other reviewers). I was a little surprised you didn't tag us but only because you're so proactive about it (for which I'm very grateful!). I don't think it's your responsibility to do all the tagging you already do do on issues and PRs (but please don't stop 🥹).

I'd be happy to help adjust/fix the automation that handles issue/PR tagging; I've already been meaning to look into it regarding tagging the loaders team (I think there is currently nothing specifically for that, only the disbanded modules team used basically only as a distro now). I was planning after off-threading hooks to ask Antoine for a pointer in the right direction.

I think we can all agree there was a misunderstanding. We generally rely on the automation for pinging and this time it let us down, so if @JakobJingleheimer can fix that, that would be great 😄 

Something that’s worth more discussion, perhaps in a new thread, is what (if any) obligations there are to revert something when requested. In this case it was a bit of a crisis averted because there was a fix possible that had no tradeoffs, but it’s easy to imagine a future case that isn’t so simple. I understand that getting a passing CI has been brutally difficult lately and that’s probably contributed to the reluctance to ever revert anything, but I don’t think that should guide our policy.

> Something that’s worth more discussion, perhaps in a new thread, is what (if any) obligations there are to revert something when requested.

This was discussed in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/34562#issuecomment-666647893, and the TL;DR is that objecting to a PR after it's merged is not an acceptable reason for a revert. (that doesn't mean we shouldn't discuss it again, I'm just linking it to give context)

> This was discussed in [#34562 (comment)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/34562#issuecomment-666647893), and the TL;DR is that objecting to a PR after it’s merged is not an acceptable reason for a revert. (that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t discuss it again, I’m just linking it to give context)

I haven’t formed an opinion as to what our policy should be regarding reverts, but I don’t see what in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/34562#issuecomment-666647893 is supposed to represent one. That revert _landed,_ firstly, and secondly it seems like the original PR probably shouldn’t have landed per our policies since it had an open objection.

I hope I never gave anyone the impression that _this_ PR shouldn’t have landed; everyone did the right thing here and no policies were violated. It would have been nice if the other groups were pinged but that’s not a _requirement,_ just something that I hope we all try to remember to do (and that we have automation to help with). This scenario is more a question of: when relevant groups didn’t get a chance to review for whatever reason, is it possible to “reopen” a PR? As in, revert what landed and then immediately open a new PR to re-land, to resume the review process as if the initial PR had never landed. That’s what I was hoping for here, so that there wouldn’t have been time pressure on me to undo what I found objectionable as quickly as possible before `main` marched on and built upon those changes. I also wouldn’t tie this specifically to whether a team was pinged or not; there are only a handful of active loaders team members, for instance, and it’s very possible that we might all have been on vacation at the same time or otherwise not monitoring our GitHub notifications for a 48-hour PR review period.

> when relevant groups didn’t get a chance to review for whatever reason, is it possible to “reopen” a PR?

The wait time in our policy (48 hours) is suppose to give a chance to the relevant groups (and anyone else) to review the PR.

> As in, revert what landed and then immediately open a new PR to re-land, to resume the review process as if the initial PR had never landed.

Well what you are describing to me looks very much like objecting to a PR after it landed, which is not something allowed per our policy.


> it’s very possible that we might all have been on vacation at the same time or otherwise not monitoring our GitHub notifications for a 48-hour PR review period.

It's possible, and the current status quo is that for that case is that your "veto power" has expired once the PR has landed, and you have to build on top of it (you can also open a PR to revert it, but it could be blocked).
It's the tradeoff the current policy makes between momentum, sufficient review, and practicality. Discussing changes to that policy should be taken to its own thread.

> I should have said "somewhat" counter-productive; it objectively was, so I'm surprised that caused upset.

@JakobJingleheimer I'm sorry if my message came off as "upset", I was not angry or upset with either you or Geoffrey. I guess I didn't communicate as well as I thought. There are no strong feelings around this from my part and I don't feel I am involved enough in the loaders effort to hold a strong opinion. 
 
I was _literally_ just making the point that if the loaders team feels strongly about this it should set up automation or get chartered by the leadership body in order to reduce future frustration.

> > in virtually every area outside of modules (and promises back then) is that the limiting factor is people willing to engage, review code and provide feedback.

> Not sure if I'm grouped into the ones who you're saying you can rely on to collab, but AFAIK, I've never not reviewed a PR on which it was requested, nor never not participated in a collaboration in which it was solicited. I especially would not ignore a request from a contributor who had collaborated with me. I hope you (and Antoine and Moshe) know I would not neglect to provide any of those for you.

Sorry for this too, and thanks! I was mostly just trying to solicit people to join the @nodejs/test_runner team 😅 

-----

As for the revert process like Antoine said, in order to revert a PR after it landed you open a revert PR which goes through the same process as any other PR. This process isn't set in stone and there have been voices in the past that made strong arguments (iirc @addaleax ) to make both landing things and reverting them easier process-wise.

I recently edited https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS and it has a comment at the top:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/71951a0e86da9253d7c422fa2520ee9143e557fa/.github/CODEOWNERS#L3-L6

Now maybe this isn’t official policy, as it’s just a comment in a file in the repo; but it feels like it _should_ be our policy. In which case then maybe I was within my rights for asking for this to be reverted.

The thing is, regardless of whether a revert or a notification are required or not, I consider them both courtesies. We’re working together and collaborating productively, and I was caught off-guard by the changes introduced here; they came very close to introducing a merge conflict in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/45869, which I was in a dayslong fight with CI to try to land. My request was essentially for more time to discuss if the changes in this PR were the best way to accomplish the goal of loading a file for the new `--test-reporter` flag, and to hopefully re-land with a better approach. If we’d reverted this and reopened a replacement and then I put a block on the replacement, that would’ve been pretty obnoxious of me and I would expect the TSC to intervene. Just because I _could_ have done such a thing isn’t a reason to not revert and reopen; there’s some element of trust involved. That’s also why I asked @MoLow to revert rather than to open the revert PR myself, since I didn’t want that to happen unless he was on board with the plan.

> If we’d reverted this and reopened a replacement and then I put a block on the replacement, that would’ve been pretty obnoxious of me and I would expect the TSC to intervene

Your original proposal was "revert what landed and then immediately open a new PR to re-land, to resume the review process as if the initial PR had never landed". In that case, you would _have to_ put a block on the PR, otherwise it would land immediately as the wait time has elapsed, CI is passing, and there was no one is blocking it. It wouldn't be obnoxious of you, it has nothing to do with trust, it's the only possible action from following the process to its logical conclusion.
Asking for a revert is fine, but Moshe was also "within his rights" to refuse. (the files would have been in the CODEOWNERS file, the bot would have pinged you and we wouldn't be discussing this at all)

IIRC the discussion around CODEOWNERS stalled because in the Node.js project, membership in teams is almost completely arbitrary (relevant people do not need to be part of a team, and people with no expertise are able to join teams). For example, I could add myself to the modules team and sign off on this PR on their behalf.

> Your original proposal was “revert what landed and then immediately open a new PR to re-land, to resume the review process as if the initial PR had never landed”. In that case, you would have to put a block on the PR, otherwise it would land immediately

The reopened one would only land when Moshe wanted it to, which presumably would have been once our discussion had run its course. It would have been no different than any open PR where someone makes a suggestion without blocking; the suggestion gets discussed for a while, maybe results in changes, and is resolved. When all such discussions are resolved, PRs land. This happens all the time without blocks needing to be used.

@cjihrig 

>  I could add myself to the modules team and sign off on this PR on their behalf.

That's only because you're a TSC member. I and everyone else who is not in the TSC would have to ask in order to join a team*.

<sub>* technically I can join teams as an org owner but I only have that power because I'm a moderator so I would not use it to do this.</sub>

-----

@GeoffreyBooth 

> Now maybe this isn’t official policy, as it’s just a comment in a file in the repo; but it feels like it should be our policy. In which case then maybe I was within my rights for asking for this to be reverted.

It isn't official policy. In this case Moshe and you both put aside the frustration of dealing with this in order to work together in good faith which is commendable. I'll share that I even posted in the moderation team slack about your behavior as a positive interaction example of de-escalating a frustrating situation, listening even though it was frustrating and behaving in an exemplary way.

I don't think we can reasonably expect people to always be as courteous as you, Moshe and the other involved parties in this example. I've seen many disagreements in the project as a collaborator and as a moderator and they _sometimes_ but not usually go this well.

That's why if the loaders team wants to sign off on these PRs I feel strongly that it should contact the TSC and ask for that adjustment to our contribution process. I'm not personally opposed to such an adjustment, I suspect other people here aren't either (and that Moshe would have actually really appreciated and benefited from an earlier review from the loaders team, which would have probably saved him time).

Our contribution process can be as frustrating as it is without having to deal with these communication issues. Expecting people to worry about PRs "slipping by" and having to monitor every PR in the project intuitively sounds super burnout inducing to me and I would not want our process to encourage that. I know this has also been an issue with streams PRs in the past.

> That's only because you're a TSC member. I and everyone else who is not in the TSC would have to ask in order to join a team*.

That is not really the point. I'm in a bunch of teams that I did not add myself to or even ask to join. Similarly, in the past we've seen people join teams very ad hoc, and as far as I know the project doesn't really have rules regulating team membership.

I'm trying to do this in a way that avoids calling any individuals out, but please take a look at team membership on GitHub and I promise you will find people in teams where they are not qualified to sign off on behalf of the team.

> That’s why if the loaders team wants to sign off on these PRs I feel strongly that it should contact the TSC and ask for that adjustment to our contribution process. I’m not personally opposed to such an adjustment, I suspect other people here aren’t either (and that Moshe would have actually really appreciated and benefited from an earlier review from the loaders team, which would have probably saved him time).

issue_context.title: Feature request: test runner reporters
issue_context.body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

The test runner currently only generates TAP output. Users would like a way to author and use reporters in a format other than TAP.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Now that the [TAP parser](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/43525) has landed, it would be nice to define some type of reporter API built on top of the parser output. Node should probably ship one reporter that is easier on the eyes than TAP, and can serve as an example of how to create a reporter.

I think at a minimum we would want an API that:

- Generates `'test'` events. This would include the test name, result, and meta information such as the test duration, comments/user logs, and error information if the test fails.
- Properly represents test nesting. This should work for both `test()` and `describe()`/`it()` style tests.
- Handle warnings that are generated for things like extraneous asynchronous activity.
- Maybe the test summary - the part that says how many tests passed, failed, etc. We may want to surface this information, but leave it up to the reporter implementer whether they want to use it, or track the counts on their own. Right now, the CLI runner reports how many test files passed or failed. A reporter author could be more interested in counting individual `test()`s, or may want to count nested tests in different ways.

### What alternatives have you considered?

There are some existing reporters on npm already. However, I think they have a few drawbacks:

- Many seem to be unmaintained or buggy.
- It is possible for Node to produce valid TAP and have a reporter consume that TAP, but still have less than ideal output. For example, a recent issue comment mentioned seeing confusing output because `tap-arc` was looking for specific fields in the TAP output. Neither Node nor `tap-arc` were wrong here and `tap-arc` has an open issue to work better with Node's test runner. It would be nice to build something that is guaranteed to work with Node's runner.
- Anything currently on npm needs to use another TAP parser to parse the test runner output. This is wasteful because Node is already doing that work in the test runner CLI.
- The existing modules generally work by piping the output of Node into another process. It would be nice to be able to run something like `node --test --test-reporter=my-reporter` and have it just work.
comments: cc: @manekinekko since you expressed interest in this. In the TAP parser PR, you initially had some colorful output that I asked you to remove. I think reporters would be the time and place to introduce that 😄

+1 for me.

A few thoughts regarding the implementation:

- we already fire some of the data through [`tapStream`](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html#class-tapstream) - we can either use that class to fire all the additional data needed for reporters to work, or use a new/different API - in that case, we might want to remove the events from `tapStream` for the sake of simplicity
- do we want to support using reporters when using `node:test` without the `--test` flag? seems like a valid use case, and we already stream TAP to `stdout`.
- another interesting use-case I know of is having multiple reporters streamed to different locations, for example, a `spec` reporter streamed to `stdout` and a `jUnit` reporter to a file. even if we do not support that directly - we should think about what API to expose that will allow that

> do we want to support using reporters when using node:test without the --test flag?

Yes, we should. Since both ways produce TAP, it should be feasible.

> another interesting use-case I know of is having multiple reporters streamed to different locations

Yes, we should support this too. We can make a new `--test-reporter` CLI flag that can be specified multiple times.

> Yes, we should support this too. We can make a new --test-reporter CLI flag that can be specified multiple times.

but how can we specify the target stream for each flag?

> but how can we specify the target stream for each flag?

To be determined 😅. There are different approaches we could try - maybe part of the CLI flag (`--test-reporter=reporter-name,stderr`), preloaded modules, etc. Maybe the simplest thing would be to only support multiple reporters via the programmatic config (`run()`). I'm open to ideas.

it should definitely be supported through `run`.
my concern is this use case is very common, and we should also provide an even simpler way to do this.
- maybe we do finally introduce a configuration file, even if it is just for test runner configuration?
- maybe each reporter can define a default destination
anyway for a first iteration supporting only `run()` for multiple reporters sounds good enough
Here is one possible way to do it: https://github.com/hapijs/lab/blob/master/API.md#multiple-reporters (also note the Custom Reporters section immediately below it)

> but how can we specify the target stream for each flag?

We should be flexible and support both `--test-reporter=abc --test-reporter=xyz` and as @cjihrig mentioned `--test-reporter=abc,xyz`

> maybe we do finally introduce a configuration file, even if it is just for test runner configuration?

Maintaining a configuration file can be hard sometimes. How about reusing `package.json` and introducing a new property?

> Maintaining a configuration file can be hard sometimes. How about reusing `package.json` and introducing a new property?

Hi, just discovering this issue. Going forward, please always tag @nodejs/modules and @nodejs/loaders for any discussion around CLI flags that load files, `package.json` stuff and config files. These are all hot topics related to module loading and tied into other designs such as the Loaders API.
